governing_thought: Acme Freight can recover three points of operating margin within 18 months by repricing twelve loss-making lanes, without cutting headcount.

slides.title: Recovering three points of margin by repricing twelve lanes
slides.subtitle: Board discussion document | September 2026
slides.notes: Open with the answer: the margin gap is a pricing problem on a small set of lanes, not a cost problem.

slides.title: Repricing twelve loss-making lanes recovers three margin points without cutting headcount
bullets: **Situation:** operating margin fell from 7.8% to 4.9% over two years while volume grew 11%
**Complication:** twelve of 140 lanes generate 80% of the operating loss
**Resolution:** reprice those lanes in two waves, 9-14% up, in line with competitors
Wave 1 (Q1-Q2): six lanes with the weakest customer switching options
Wave 2 (Q3-Q4): six lanes tied to contract renewals
**Decision today:** approve Wave 1 pricing and the customer communication plan
slides.source: Source: Acme Freight lane P&L, FY2024-FY2026; team analysis
slides.notes: This is the whole deck on one page. If the board reads nothing else, it reads this.

slides.title: Twelve of 140 lanes generate 80% of the operating loss
slides.source: Source: Acme Freight lane P&L, FY2026 year to date; n = 140 active lanes
slides.notes: The concentration is the insight: fixing a small set of lanes fixes most of the problem.

slides.title: Competitors already charge 9-14% more on these lanes, so the increase is defensible

columns.heading: What we charge today
bullets: $2.41 per mile average on the twelve lanes

columns.heading: What the market charges
bullets: $2.63-$2.75 per mile from the three nearest competitors
Two competitors repriced in the last nine months

slides.source: Source: broker rate benchmarks, Q2 2026; competitor tariff filings
slides.notes: Anticipate the objection that customers will leave; the market has already moved.

slides.title: A two-wave rollout captures 60% of the upside in the first two quarters
slides.source: Source: team pricing model; assumes 5% volume attrition on repriced lanes
slides.notes: The attrition assumption is conservative; the sensitivity is in the appendix.

slides.quote: We would pay more on these lanes for guaranteed capacity. What we will not accept is surprise surcharges.
slides.notes: Close on the customer voice: price certainty matters more than price level.
